A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BridgeRemoval, and their text, equations, figures, and tables are readable. The supplied v1 ends with references despite an appendix cross-reference; v4 includes Appendices A–F. The supplied contents support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5.1 and Figures 2–4 report original qualitative experiments comparing BridgeRemoval with GenOmnimatte, ROSE, and VACE, although no quantitative results are provided.

after.justification: Sections 5.2–5.5 and Appendices C–E report original quantitative benchmarks, a user study, ablations, and qualitative failure cases.

M1.justification: Section 4.4 replaces background-only multiplicative modulation with mask-conditioned spatial scale and shift, generated through a 3D convolution and separate 1×1×1 projections. Equation 13 also adds the missing normalization factor multiplying predicted velocity. These change the specified component and inference calculation; the backbone and bridge training objective remain.

E1.justification: V4 adds explicit evaluation on DAVIS and the new 150-video BridgeRemoval-Bench, comprising stock, generated, and social-media videos with varied orientations and object configurations. V1 provides selected qualitative examples without a defined evaluation dataset. The approximately 47,000-pair training collection remains unchanged.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates ROSE, VACE, and GenOmnimatte qualitatively. V4 retains these and adds Ditto, ICVE, and the Zi et al. (2025b) method labeled Senoria in Tables 1–2 and Senorita in Tables 5–6. All six participate in the new quantitative comparisons.

E3.justification: V4 introduces CLIP-T/F, unmasked-region PSNR/MSE/LPIPS, VBench, and runtime evaluation, plus a three-criterion, five-point user study with 24 participants and 1,440 evaluations. It also tests 10–50 inference steps. The previously stated training configuration and default 50-step inference setting are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds an AMM on/off comparison for a bus occupying approximately 80% of the frame and an inference-step sensitivity study with numerical and visual evidence. Appendix E adds a comparative fast-motion failure case. V1 contains no corresponding ablations or explicit failure analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V4's participant and rating counts describe its new study's sample size, without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V4 adds quantitative results absent from v1, including BridgeRemoval PSNR values of 28.2154 on DAVIS and 33.2394 on BridgeRemoval-Bench, and a user-study average of 4.57 versus GenOmnimatte's 3.57. Tables 4–6 add step-sensitivity and VBench results, while qualitative examples are replaced and expanded. These are newly reported evaluations, not matched-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V4 adds Appendix B's Gaussian bridge marginal derivation, analytic guidance term, and claimed equivalence between velocity and score matching; v1 contains no supplied proofs. Equation 13's inversion is also corrected. These are substantial mathematical additions, although the schedule reduction and score-matching equivalence remain incompletely justified.

C1.justification: The introduction adds BridgeRemoval-Bench as an explicit contribution, expanding the work beyond its method contributions. The conclusion drops v1's specific claim concerning removal of unmasked shadows. The central bridge formulation, AMM, and visual-quality/temporal-consistency claims remain.

C2.justification: V4 introduces substantive interpretations of the removal-versus-background-fidelity trade-off across inference steps, explains why VBench may not measure successful object removal, and acknowledges failures on rapidly moving objects. V1's explanation of implicit shadow removal through broader contextual reasoning is removed.

D1.justification: V4 adds benchmark mask/caption construction details, L20X inference hardware, schedule-table precomputation, convolutional AMM details, and a project-page pointer. The main training disclosures—including backbone, clip length, resolutions, optimizer, schedule, training budget, and H100 hardware—were already present in v1.

R1.justification: V4 adds references supporting the new comparators, benchmark metrics, FiLM modulation, and mathematical discussion, and explicitly identifies AMM's FiLM inspiration. The related-work discussion and central positioning against noise-initialized diffusion remain largely unchanged; several other reference edits merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The title, main section order, and most introductory and related-work prose are retained. V4 renames Section 4, revises explanatory passages, expands experimental subheadings and appendix cross-references, and updates the author block. Much of the additional prose documents new scientific material rather than restructuring the existing narrative.

P2.justification: V4 retains the framework diagram but replaces v1's three qualitative galleries and adds a user-study chart, AMM and inference-step visualizations, and a failure-case figure. Six tables and additional appendix algorithm panels substantially expand the presentation. Large qualitative figures no longer interrupt the reference list.

improvement.justification: V1's broad performance claims rely on selected qualitative examples. V4 substantially strengthens their assessability through quantitative comparisons, additional baselines, a user study, component and step ablations, and explicit failure analysis. It also corrects Equation 13. The new theoretical appendix leaves important derivation gaps, and statistical uncertainty remains unreported, but the substantial improvement in empirical support and disclosure of limitations outweighs these weaknesses.
